entities.name: Sahih al-Bukhari
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The most authoritative hadith collection in Sunni Islam, compiled by Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (810–870 CE) over 16 years of travel and research. From an estimated 600,000 hadith traditions he heard, al-Bukhari selected 7,275 (approximately 2,602 without repetitions) based on rigorous criteria of isnad (chain of transmission) verification — each narrator in the chain had to be documented as trustworthy, have met the previous narrator, and have a reliable memory.

Organized into 97 books covering subjects from revelation and faith to medicine and dress, Sahih al-Bukhari is considered second only to the Qur'an in authority. Its methodology of source criticism ('ilm al-rijal) represents one of the most systematic approaches to evaluating historical testimony in pre-modern scholarship.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sahih al-Bukhari's rigorous methodology of source criticism ('ilm al-rijal) set a precedent for evaluating historical testimony in Islamic scholarship and beyond, influencing the development of hadith studies and Islamic law. Its authority has been recognized by scholars across centuries.
